findings.existing_code: (`meta skuid ghrunner fib daddr type local drop` in an `output` hook chain). Because
findings.description: The preferred host-isolation control in D6/A11/O4 (`meta skuid ghrunner fib daddr type local drop`) breaks name resolution inside every runner container on a default Ubuntu 24.04 host. With slirp4netns the container's resolver is 10.0.2.3, and the slirp4netns process (running as `ghrunner`) forwards those queries to the host's configured nameserver, which under systemd-resolved is the loopback stub 127.0.0.53. That destination is `fib type local`, so the rule drops all container DNS. The O4 probe check would still pass (everything is unreachable, including DNS), and the first symptom is the O6 dry run failing on `actions/checkout` / `uv` network errors with no pointer back to the rule. The podman-5 `pasta:--no-map-gw` alternative has the same exposure. Fix: carve out the stub resolver (`meta skuid ghrunner ip daddr 127.0.0.53 udp dport 53 accept` and the tcp twin, placed before the drop), or point the containers at an external resolver (`--dns 1.1.1.1` in ExecStart, pinned by test), and add a positive O4 check (`podman exec gx10-runner-1 getent hosts api.github.com` succeeds) so the isolation proof also demonstrates the runner still works.
findings.resolution: Add a DNS carve-out (or `--dns` pin) to D6/A11 and O4, plus a positive reachability check for api.github.com in O4.

findings.existing_code: services bind, while leaving internet egress intact. Installing the rule is operator-only.
findings.description: D6 and A11 only consider services on the GX10 itself. Moving PR execution from GitHub-hosted VMs to this host also gives same-repository PR code (including Dependabot and agent branches, per A10) a network position inside the operator's LAN and Tailscale tailnet: `fib daddr type local` matches only the host's own addresses, so other machines on 192.168/10.x and the 100.64.0.0/10 tailnet (the operator's workstation, NAS, other coordinator deployments) become reachable from a runner, which was never true from `ubuntu-latest`. The design should either extend the rule to drop `ghrunner` traffic to RFC1918 and 100.64.0.0/10 destinations (with the same DNS carve-out as finding 1) or record the lateral-reach residual explicitly in the Risks table and A11, and O4 should probe one non-host LAN/tailnet address.
findings.resolution: Extend the nftables rule to private/CGNAT ranges or document the lateral-reach residual and probe it in O4.

findings.existing_code: - `labels` = manifest `self_hosted_labels`, read from the env file that the install docs
findings.description: D5 has the mint script pass the full manifest set `[self-hosted, linux, ARM64, gx10]` as the `labels` field of `generate-jitconfig`, and the spec scenario 'JIT labels match the routing labels' pins equality. The `labels` field of that endpoint is for custom labels; `self-hosted`, the OS label (`Linux`) and the architecture label (`ARM64`) are default labels the runner service assigns itself, and submitting reserved default labels as custom labels is rejected or silently de-duplicated depending on the API version, so the first real mint in O4 may fail with a 422 while every stubbed test is green. The contract should distinguish custom labels (`gx10`) from the default labels the runner adds, have the script send only the custom subset, and have the test assert that `custom ∪ defaults == routing.self_hosted_labels` (case-insensitively, since GitHub emits `Linux`).
findings.resolution: Split `self_hosted_labels` into default and custom labels in D5/spec/test 3.3; send only custom labels to the JIT endpoint.

findings.existing_code: - [ ] O1 Create the dedicated host user and enable linger *(outcome 4, host half)*
findings.description: A9 and D6 make per-container `--cpus` / `--memory` limits mandatory because the ri-08 daemon shares the host, but rootless podman can only enforce them if the cpu, memory and pids cgroup v2 controllers are delegated to `ghrunner`'s user slice. Ubuntu's default `user@.service` delegation does not reliably include `cpu`/`cpuset`; when it is missing, podman logs a warning and runs the container with no CPU limit, and nothing in O1–O4 would notice. O1 should verify delegation (`cat /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-$(id -u ghrunner).slice/cgroup.controllers` lists `cpu memory pids`) and, if not, add the `user@.service.d/delegate.conf` drop-in as an operator step; O4 should confirm `podman inspect` reports the configured `NanoCpus`/`Memory`.
findings.resolution: Add a controller-delegation check and drop-in to O1 and a limit-enforcement check to O4.
